entry.title: My current cybersecurity learning roadmap
entry.content:
My current roadmap is built around consistent, hands-on practice.

I split my study into four tracks: networking (CCNA topics), Linux operations, AWS fundamentals, and web security labs.

Instead of studying topics in isolation, I combine them in lab scenarios and document what works, what fails, and what I need to improve next.
entry.summary: A practical roadmap across networking, Linux, cloud, and security operations.

entry.title: How I use PortSwigger labs for web security practice

link.title: How I use PortSwigger labs for web security practice

entry.content:
PortSwigger labs help me connect theory with practical exploitation and mitigation.

My workflow is simple:

  1. Reproduce the vulnerable behavior.
  2. Confirm the root cause in HTTP requests and responses.
  3. Write down how to fix or prevent it.
  4. Re-test to verify understanding.

This process is helping me improve how I analyze authentication, access control, and session-related issues.
entry.summary: My workflow for learning web vulnerabilities with repeatable testing and notes.

entry.title: Home lab notes: Linux, Docker, and cloud practice

link.title: Home lab notes: Linux, Docker, and cloud practice

entry.content:
My home lab is where I test most ideas before using them in bigger environments.

I regularly use Linux VMs, Docker containers, and AWS EC2 instances to practice service deployment, system hardening, and troubleshooting.

The goal is not just to make things work once, but to build a repeatable workflow I can explain clearly.
entry.summary: A snapshot of my home lab setup and why it is central to my cybersecurity learning.
